This combination of long-dated funding and multi-year capital spending underlines UPS's push toward higher-value, specialized logistics services and a more resilient global network.

We'll now examine how UPS's more than US$2.00 billion push into international and healthcare logistics reshapes its existing investment narrative.

United Parcel Service Investment Narrative Recap

To own UPS, you need to believe its shift toward higher-value, international and healthcare logistics can offset weaker parcel cycles, Amazon volume cuts, and a heavy dividend burden. The new US$325.11 million, 2076 floating-rate note and more than US$2.00 billion of planned capex marginally support this thesis near term, but they do not materially change the key catalyst of executing the Network of the Future, or the main risk of margins being squeezed during that transition.

The most relevant recent development here is UPS's decision to hold its quarterly dividend at US$1.64 per share, with payout at about 91% of expected 2026 adjusted earnings. Combined with funding part of the dividend via borrowing, this underscores how tight financial flexibility is as UPS pursues network reconfiguration and international expansion, sharpening the trade off between funding growth projects and maintaining shareholder returns.

title: Billionaires Are Quietly Loading Up on Amazon While It Trades Like a Value Stock
detail:
Billionaires Are Quietly Loading Up on Amazon While It Trades Like a Value Stock
Adam Spatacco, The Motley Fool
Wed, August 26, 2026 at 11:50 AM EDT 6 min read
AMZN
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Recent 13F filings reveal that a flurry of top hedge fund managers bought the same "Magnificent Seven" stock during the second quarter: Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN). These purchases by Stanley Druckenmiller, Peter Thiel, Seth Klarman, and David Tepper are more than coincidental portfolio adjustments.

I think this collective bet on Amazon underscores a recognition that the company is evolving far beyond its e-commerce roots into a platform business positioned for durable growth. What unites their thinking is a keen focus on emerging businesses that compound through technological leverage, cash generation, and competitive advantages that others in the big tech ecosystem struggle to replicate at scale.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Converging on diversification

These hedge fund managers all share a preference for companies that blend defensive cash flow with offensive growth engines. Druckenmiller has long favored asymmetric upside in technology leaders while Thiel prioritizes network effects and monopoly-like businesses. Klarman tends to seek a margin of safety in undervalued assets while Tepper is always on the hunt for cyclical recoveries with secular tailwinds. Amazon satisfies each of these criteria.

Amazon's strength in artificial intelligence (AI) stems from its cloud computing division, Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS provides a computational backbone for training and deploying AI models at a global scale. Beyond this, Amazon's logistics network, advertising platform, and subscription services (Prime) create a reinforcing ecosystem: Data from retail and enterprise customers improves ad targeting, fulfillment efficiency lowers delivery costs, and cloud infrastructure monetizes the resulting intelligence.

The company's diversification is the subtle strength here. Retail shoppers generate order volume, which helps Amazon build relationships with its customers. Advertising extracts high-margin revenue from these relationships while AWS delivers operating leverage. As a result, the company is able to reinvest in emerging efforts across robotics and custom silicon -- helping reduce dependency on external suppliers and manufacturers. Amazon's multi-legged stool reduces the risk of a single point of failure while amplifying returns.

The simultaneous buying by all these billionaire investors suggests they saw the last few months as a window where the market remained distracted by near-term retail pressures from inflation, ultimately obscuring the accelerating contribution from higher-margin, technology-enabled segments.

title: Top Midday Stories: Meta to Pay Up to $16.68 Billion to Settle Teen Harm Case With States; Victory Capital to Buy First Eagle for $7 Billion
detail:
PREMIUM
Top Midday Stories: Meta to Pay Up to $16.68 Billion to Settle Teen Harm Case With States; Victory Capital to Buy First Eagle for $7 Billion
MT Newswires
Wed, August 26, 2026 at 11:43 AM EDT 4 min read
NVDA
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

All three major US stock indexes were down slightly in late-morning trading Wednesday, as market participants took in the latest inflation data and prepared for Nvidia (NVDA) to release its earnings results after markets close.

The personal consumption expenditures index, a measure of inflation, rose by 0.2% in July, faster than the 0.1% gain expected in a survey conducted by Bloomberg as of 6:10 am ET and following a 0.1% drop in June. The July figure keeps the year-over-year rate at 3.7%. The core PCE index, which excludes food and energy prices, increased by 0.2%, as expected and following a 0.1% gain in June. The year-over-year rate remained at 3.3% in the month.

Separately, US gross domestic product rose by 1.5% in Q2, unrevised from the advance estimate released last month and matching the consensus estimate from a Bloomberg survey as of 6:10 am ET.

In company news, Meta Platforms (META) has agreed to pay a maximum of $16.68 billion to resolve claims brought by several US states that the tech giant used its platforms to "ensnare" youth and teens, according to a Wednesday filing in federal court. The consent agreement's injunctive relief also requires Meta to take several steps to regulate children's usage of its social media platforms, including daily limits and nighttime blocks. In a separate release, Meta said the agreement includes a payment of about $18 billion to be distributed in annual installments over a 10-year period. Plaintiff states will receive about $12.7 billion over the decade, while the remaining roughly 30%, or $5.3 billion, will be released if Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) YouTube and TikTok "implement a one-hour Daily Limit, Night Mode, and Age assurance measures," and they each pay an amount equal to the 30% figure. Meta shares were up 2.1% around midday. Alphabet's Class C and Class A shares were down 1.1% and 1.2%, respectively.

Victory Capital (VCTR) signed a definitive agreement to acquire First Eagle Investments from Genstar Capital and First Eagle employees for about $7 billion, Victory said Wednesday. Victory will pay about $4.4 billion in cash, $2 billion in newly issued shares and will assume $575 million of First Eagle's existing 7.25% senior secured notes due 2032, the company said. The deal is expected to close in Q1 2027, at which point Genstar will own a 14.6% stake in Victory, the company said. Victory Capital shares were up 6.3%.

Intuit (INTU) reported fiscal Q4 adjusted earnings late Tuesday of $4.03 per diluted share, up from $2.75 a year earlier and above the FactSet consensus of $3.58. Fiscal Q4 revenue was $4.35 billion, up from $3.83 billion a year ago and above the FactSet consensus of $4.27 billion. For fiscal Q1, the company expects adjusted EPS of $2.44 to $2.48 on revenue of $4.29 billion to $4.31 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expect $4.04 and $4.35 billion, respectively. For fiscal 2027, Intuit expects adjusted EPS of $22.88 to $23.12 on revenue of $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion. Analysts expect $27.34 and $23.70 billion, respectively. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $1.38 per share from $1.20, payable on Oct. 16. Intuit shares were down 4.5%.

Boston Scientific (BSX) identified a cybersecurity incident that affected some of its IT systems and led to global disruptions in operations, the company said Wednesday in a regulatory filing. Boston Scientific shares were down 4.7%.

Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet's Google are in talks with Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI over revenue-sharing deals for hosting Moonshot's Kimi K3 model, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing sources familiar with the matter. Separately, Amazon plans to expand fulfillment capacity, same-day delivery and its logistics network in Canada despite escalating trade tensions between the US and Canada, Business Insider reported Wednesday, citing internal company documents. Lastly, Amazon's AWS unit is acquiring DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based company behind the open-source analytical database DuckDB, for an undisclosed sum, Amazon said. The deal is expected to close shortly, Amazon said. Shares of Amazon were down 0.6%, and Microsoft was up 0.7%.

Bath & Body Works Q2 Earnings Call Highlights

Key Points

Interested in Bath & Body Works, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Q2 results exceeded expectations: Net sales fell 2.3% to $1.5 billion, but adjusted EPS reached $0.62, including an $80 million tariff refund. Excluding the refund, EPS was $0.31, still above the high end of guidance.

Sales remain pressured despite strategic progress: U.S. and Canadian store sales declined 5.4%, while direct sales rose 3% and international and other revenue increased 24.9%. Product launches, digital improvements, Amazon expansion and the Ulta rollout showed traction, though management said gains were not yet broad enough to reverse the overall trend.

Outlook and investments improved: Full-year sales guidance was narrowed to a 2.5%–4% decline, while adjusted EPS guidance increased to $2.60–$2.80. The company plans to invest an additional $35 million in its Consumer First Formula strategy, targets $200 million in 2026 savings and expects approximately $650 million in free cash flow.

Bath & Body Works Stock Surged Despite Falling Sales—Here's Why

Bath & Body Works (NYSE:BBWI) reported second-quarter results that exceeded its prior outlook, though sales remained under pressure as the retailer invests in product innovation, marketing, digital capabilities and expanded distribution to support a planned return to revenue growth in 2027.

Net sales for the second quarter totaled $1.5 billion, down 2.3% from a year earlier. The result was better than the company's guidance for a decline of 3% to 5%. Adjusted earnings per diluted share were $0.62, above the prior outlook of $0.20 to $0.25.

Bath & Body Works Hits Multi-Year Lows: Bargain or Trap?

The earnings figure included approximately $80 million in tariff refunds received during the quarter. Excluding that benefit, adjusted EPS would have been $0.31, or $0.06 above the high end of the company's guidance range, according to Chief Executive Officer Daniel Heaf.

Sales trends and category performance

Interim Chief Financial Officer Tom Javitch said the company entered its June semiannual sale with less clearance inventory than it had a year earlier. While the inventory position was healthier for the brand, it reduced second-quarter sales by about one percentage point and affected all categories.

Body care sales declined by the mid-single digits, though the category improved sequentially from the first quarter.

Home fragrance sales declined by the low single digits, reflecting a strategic reduction in Halloween assortment and reduced clearance product. Strength in single-wick candles and Wallflower heaters partly offset those pressures.

Soaps and sanitizers were flat, with newer moisturizing and revitalizing soap formulas supporting performance.

Affirm (AFRM) is positioned for a potential fiscal Q4 2026 gross merchandise volume beat, but management could issue a conservative fiscal 2027 outlook due to Prime Day timing, Morgan Stanley said in a note Wednesday.

The investment firm said Bloomberg observed-sales data indicate Affirm's fiscal Q4 GMV growth could be close to 34%, above consensus of about 29%, while investors are increasingly focused on potential spending softness in August following strong July activity.

For fiscal Q1 and fiscal 2027, investors seem to expect initial GMV growth guidance of about 27%, below consensus estimates of 28.5% and 29%, respectively, with the absence of a Prime Day event in fiscal Q1 likely resulting in a potential 3- to 4-percentage-point drag from the prior year, according to the note.

The firm said it remained confident in Affirm's underlying business, citing its Amazon (AMZN) and Shopify (SHOP) distribution, broad product offering and execution.

Morgan Stanley maintained its equal-weight rating on Affirm and raised its price target to $80 from $79.

Affirm shares were down 1.5% in Wednesday trading.

title: Is IBM Stock A Bargain After Its 28% Drawdown?
detail:
Is IBM Stock A Bargain After Its 28% Drawdown?
Trefis Team
Wed, August 26, 2026 at 9:21 AM EDT 3 min read
ACN
QTWO
ORCL-PD
IBM
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by ArtsyBee on Pixabay

The software line that fell hardest at IBM is the one its upside case runs through, and the capacity behind it is already installed.

International Business Machines (IBM) stock has gone almost nowhere over the past twelve months, down 0.7%, and it trades about 28% below its 52-week high after a fiscal Q2 2026 that fell short of the company's own expectations. The easy read is that the mainframe franchise is finally cracking. The company's disclosures offer a different perspective: the transaction software line that weighed on quarterly performance is also where management sees its primary operating leverage.

Where The Mainframe Software Budget Actually Went

In fiscal Q2 2026, transaction processing revenue, the software that rides on the mainframe, fell 9% year over year, and mainframe hardware fell 42% against a prior-year launch quarter that had grown 70%. Management's account is specific: clients redirected budget toward supply-constrained servers, storage, and memory ahead of expected price increases, and tens of large deals, some of them enterprise license agreements, slipped as a result. About a third of those deals closed within three weeks of the quarter ending, against a normal expectation of two-thirds to three-quarters over six months, which management calls a good indication, not yet full evidence, that this was deferral and not destruction.

IBM Ships The Hardware First And Bills The Software Later

The distinction matters because of how the mainframe monetizes. Five quarters into the z17 program, IBM sits at nearly 130% program to program, worth about $1 billion more of mainframe revenue than the z16 cycle at the same point, plus more than $3 billion more of software stack on top, by management's account. None of that is a forecast. Over 140 million MIPS of installed mainframe capacity are running in the field, clients representing 85% of them are holding or adding capacity, and the more capacity in the market, the company says, the more transaction processing there is to monetize later.

Against IBM's overall revenue base, five quarters of that accumulated stack matters at the margin without remaking the company; the upside case is the capacity now in place, not the revenue already earned. Management is protecting profitability through the wait: after taking 2026 revenue growth down to 4% to 5%, it held its operating pretax margin commitment at 100 basis points of expansion and free cash flow growth at about $1 billion. Cash generation that survives a marked-down top line is the kind of quality the Trefis High Quality Portfolio holds.
